Baseline EEG was abnormal in 55% of cases (12 EA2, 9 FHM1).

claims.object_text: lateralized intermittent slowing, mainly affecting the temporal region
claims.quote: The most common finding was a lateralized intermittent slowing, mainly affecting the temporal region.

claims.object_text: slowing more pronounced after a recent attack and persistent during follow-up
claims.quote: Slowing was more pronounced after a recent attack but was consistently detected in the majority of patients also during the follow-up.
Interictal epileptic discharges (IEDs) were detected in eight patients (7 EA2,1 FHM1).

claims.object_text: EEG abnormalities and especially IEDs associated with younger age and earlier disease onset
claims.quote: EEG abnormalities and especially IEDs were significantly associated with younger age at examination (16 ± 9 vs 43 ± 21 years in those without epileptic changes, p = 0.003) and with earlier onset of disease (1 (1-2) vs 12 (5-45) years, p = 0.0009).

claims.object_text: EEG abnormalities more prevalent than in CACNA1A-negative phenocopies
claims.quote: EEG findings in CACNA1A-negative phenocopies (n = 15) were largely unremarkable (p = 0.03 in the comparison with CACNA1A patients).

claims.object_text: age-dependent effect with more severe impairment when P/Q channel dysfunction manifests early in life
claims.quote: Our findings underpin an age-dependent effect of CACNA1A variants, with a more severe impairment when P/Q channel dysfunction manifests early in life.
